subject: horned frog
title: This Frog Bites Like a Mammal Predator and Eats Prey Its Own Size

scenes.text: Scientists measured one frog's bite, and it led them to a frog that ate dinosaurs.
The South American horned frog sits still with a huge mouth, and waits.
It ambushes animals as large as itself: snakes, rodents and other frogs.
A small horned frog bites with about 30 newtons. The biggest are calculated at nearly 500.
That's like 50 litres of water on your fingertip, as strong as mammals with heads that size.
Scaled up, its giant extinct cousin Beelzebufo bit like a wolf, enough to grab baby dinosaurs.

description:
South American horned frogs bite as hard as mammal and reptile predators with heads the same size.
In a 2017 Scientific Reports study, researchers measured a small horned frog (head about 4.5 cm wide) biting with 30 newtons and calculated almost 500 N for the largest ones (head up to 10 cm). Horned frogs ambush prey as large as themselves. Scaling up, the team estimated that Beelzebufo, a giant frog that lived in Madagascar about 68 million years ago, bit with up to 2,200 N, comparable to wolves and female tigers, enough to subdue small and young dinosaurs.
Which animal's bite would you least want to test?
